Synopsis:
Ahead of the Saxony-Anhalt state election, the AfD leads polls and may seize its first state-level government. The article traces eastern German ambivalence toward Russia to decades of Soviet military presence under the GDR, economic trauma post-reunification, and resentment at being politically dismissed. The AfD capitalises on nostalgia for cheap Russian energy and skepticism of Berlin's pro-Ukraine stance. The Merz coalition frames AfD sympathies as a security threat, citing Russian hybrid warfare. The core tension: eastern voters prioritise economic stability and détente over geopolitical alignment with the West.
